note:
End-to-end paths. The first group is the intended run. The second tests the author's instruction that a seizure occurs regardless of how well the case is being managed. The third walks the do-nothing trajectory to the arrest, which is the path a frozen learner sees. The fourth is every deterioration branch and its rescue, including a rescue that arrives too late. The fifth is physostigmine while the QRS is wide and after she has stabilized, which is the case. Then the other harmful actions, the prerequisites (including the one that must not halt), the coverage groups, the two-flag resolution requirement, and a handoff from three different phases.

Since 5 September 2026 a sixth group tests the arrow that takes a patient who receives sodium bicarbonate in the arrival phase straight to the narrowing phase: the escape, the flawless run with and without the drug, the boundary at 230 seconds rather than 240, and how it interacts with physostigmine in both orders.

A seventh group covers amiodarone into the wide-complex rhythm, which arrests her instantaneously, and the two orderings against the bicarbonate rescue.

27 October 2026, physician review (Aakash Setty): the escape group is inverted (DIPH-01), the amiodarone group now expects a fall in pressure rather than an arrest (DIPH-12), and new groups cover the one-time relapse (DIPH-09), phenytoin's consequence (DIPH-23) and propranolol (DIPH-27).

scenarios.name: Intended path: monitor, access, glucose, ECG, benzodiazepine for the seizure, bicarbonate, cooling, toxicology, handoff
scenarios.note: They are laboratory orders rather than examinations because an examination is never state-changing: the engine does not re-evaluate the transition list after one, so a phase cannot be advanced by palpating an abdomen. The scenario runner agreed with the engine about this only from 5 September 2026.

scenarios.name: Intended path reaches the stabilized phase before any handoff
scenarios.note:
Bicarbonate narrows the QRS ten seconds after it is given, then cooling and toxicology are the two flags the stabilized phase requires.

The trailing laboratory order is load-bearing rather than decorative: the stabilizing-to-stabilized rule is instantaneous, an instantaneous rule is evaluated on a state-changing action or a clock event, and the action before it was the one that entered the phase. In play there is always a next event; in a scenario file there is not unless you write one.

scenarios.name: A benzodiazepine and bicarbonate before the seizure no longer prevent it
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-01 (Aakash Setty, 27 October 2026) deleted the escape. Both drugs before four minutes no longer prevent the seizure: it fires at 240 seconds in every run, as the case author wrote.

scenarios.name: Doing nothing at all reaches the seizure at four minutes
scenarios.note: The unguarded transition. Nothing the resident does prevents it and nothing is required to reach it.

scenarios.name: A flawless first four minutes WITHOUT bicarbonate still reaches the seizure
scenarios.note: The author's instruction. Everything correct, and the seizure fires on the clock exactly as she wrote it.

scenarios.name: Doing nothing at all: seizure, then wide complex, then arrest
scenarios.note: The whole clock path with no action taken. This is the trajectory section 14.2c prints and it ends in a dead patient.

scenarios.name: Seizure treated and conduction never treated: arrest by the longer road
scenarios.note: Post-ictal at 180 seconds into the wide-complex phase, then 120 more to the arrest.

scenarios.name: Untreated seizure reaches the wide-complex phase
Bicarbonate with a benzodiazepine rescues the wide-complex phase inside the window
scenarios.note: v0.18a: she is still convulsing in this phase when she reaches it from the seizure, and bicarbonate is not an anticonvulsant, so the rescue needs both drugs.

scenarios.name: The bicarbonate infusion with a benzodiazepine also rescues it
scenarios.note: The infusion sets the same flag as the bolus, so a resident who reaches only for the drip is not treated as having withheld bicarbonate.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate alone in the wide-complex phase narrows the complexes and leaves her seizing
scenarios.note: v0.18a. Before this review she stayed in the wide-complex phase at a rate of 180 after the drug that treats it, with no exit but the handoff. She now returns to the seizing phase, and the nurse's prompt for an anticonvulsant is still live.

scenarios.name: A benzodiazepine after bicarbonate alone still reaches stabilizing
Propofol counts as the anticonvulsant in the wide-complex rescue
scenarios.note: v0.18a. The seizing phase already accepted propofol as ending the convulsion. The rescue guards now use the same definition.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate one second too late does not rescue it
scenarios.note: Deterioration is all-or-nothing. The arrest fires at 120 seconds and the drug arrives after it.

scenarios.name: Untreated conduction from the post-ictal phase reaches the wide-complex phase
Physostigmine before the ECG halts the case
scenarios.note: The tag evaluates to harmful because no ECG has resulted, and a harmful action bypasses every transition rule.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine after the ECG halts the case while the QRS is wide
scenarios.note: v0.18a. The tag used to depend on whether the ECG had resulted, so reading the tracing and then giving the drug the tracing forbids was scored more leniently than not reading it. It now depends on the phase: harmful in every phase in which the QRS is wide.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine after she has stabilized is discouraged and does not halt the case
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-02: physostigmine is harmful through the narrowing phase and discouraged only once she has stabilized. This run reaches the stabilized phase first.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine one action after the ECG halts the case
scenarios.note: v0.18a. This scenario asserted the opposite before the review, because the tag gated on the ECG having resulted. It now gates on the phase, so the timing of the tracing no longer matters.

scenarios.name: Flumazenil after a benzodiazepine halts the case
Flumazenil with no benzodiazepine on board is discouraged and does not halt the case
scenarios.note: v0.18a. With nothing to reverse, the harm is a lower seizure threshold rather than a withdrawal seizure, so it is scored discouraged. Clinical sign-off needed.

scenarios.name: A further dose of diphenhydramine halts the case
Procainamide in the wide-complex phase halts the case
Procainamide before the wide-complex phase halts the case
scenarios.note: v0.18a. Procainamide is a sodium-channel blocker and her QRS is already 132 milliseconds on arrival, so it is harmful in every phase until she has stabilized.

scenarios.name: An intravenous drug with no line is blocked and changes nothing
scenarios.note: The catalog's vascular-access prerequisite. The attempt is logged, the flag is not set, and the phase does not move.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine with no line is blocked and does not halt the case
scenarios.note: A blocked harmful action must not halt. This is the one scenario in the pack whose failure would be silent and lethal to the lesson.

scenarios.name: Intubation without sedation and paralysis is blocked
Intubation after induction and paralysis proceeds
scenarios.note: Intubation does not change the phase in this case, by design. It sets a flag and moves the saturation.

scenarios.name: Midazolam terminates the seizure, through the lorazepam coverage
Ringer's carries the same tag as saline, through the crystalloid group
Vancomycin carries the same tag as ceftriaxone, through the antibiotic coverage
Magnesium through the bolus entry is the same act as through the plain entry
Cooling without toxicology does not reach the stabilized phase
scenarios.note: Both flags are required. This is the half of the conjunction that is easy to get wrong.

scenarios.name: Toxicology without cooling does not reach the stabilized phase
A handoff from the arrival phase completes the case
A handoff during the seizure completes the case
scenarios.note: Poor practice and permitted. The handoff rule is first in every transition list, so it is never overtaken by a clinical rule in the same step.

scenarios.name: A handoff from the wide-complex phase completes the case
A flawless first four minutes with both drugs still seizes at four minutes
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-01. Before 27 October 2026 this run escaped the seizure. The best run now convulses at four minutes, as the case author wrote, and recovers from the post-ictal phase on the flags already set.

scenarios.name: Both drugs, then the seizure, then the narrowing phase from the post-ictal phase
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-01. The seizure fires at 240 whatever was given. The benzodiazepine already on board ends it on the next event, and the bicarbonate then carries her out of the post-ictal phase ten seconds later. The laboratory order is the event an instantaneous rule needs.

scenarios.name: Both drugs just before the seizure are not wasted
scenarios.note: Both drugs are in, the seizure fires on the clock, the benzodiazepine flag ends it and the bicarbonate flag carries her out of the post-ictal phase. Since DIPH-01 there is no escape in any timing. The two laboratory orders are the events the instantaneous rules need.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine in the narrowing phase halts the case
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-02 closes the gap this scenario used to record: the narrowing phase still has a QRS of 104 ms, so physostigmine there halts the case.

scenarios.name: Physostigmine after both drugs on arrival halts the case
scenarios.note: Both drugs on arrival do not change physostigmine's tag, which depends on the phase. The arrival QRS is 132 ms.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate alone does not escape the seizure
scenarios.note: Since DIPH-01 nothing escapes the seizure. Kept as a check that the clock fires with one drug given.

scenarios.name: A benzodiazepine alone does not escape it either
scenarios.note: Since DIPH-01 nothing escapes the seizure. Kept as a check that the clock fires with one drug given.

scenarios.name: Amiodarone in the wide-complex rhythm drops her pressure and does not arrest her
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-12 (Aakash Setty, 27 October 2026): the instant arrest is replaced by a fall of 20 systolic and 12 diastolic ten seconds after the drug, while she is in this rhythm.

scenarios.name: Amiodarone outside that rhythm is discouraged and nothing happens
scenarios.note: Discouraged everywhere, and its pressure effect acts only in the wide-complex rhythm. Signed as authored in physician review DIPH-26.

scenarios.name: Amiodarone with bicarbonate: the bicarbonate still works
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-12. With no arrest arrow, bicarbonate alone narrows the rhythm and returns her to the seizing phase, as it does without amiodarone.

scenarios.name: Amiodarone after the wide-complex rescue has fired does nothing
scenarios.note: Once she is out of the wide-complex phase, amiodarone is discouraged and its pressure effect does not act.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate during the seizure with no anticonvulsant relapses into the wide-complex rhythm
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-09 (Aakash Setty, 27 October 2026), option B. The seizing phase is entered at 240 seconds and the relapse fires 180 seconds later.

scenarios.name: After the relapse, the earlier bicarbonate does not narrow the rhythm again
scenarios.note: DIPH-09. The relapse needs a fresh dose. No second arrest clock is authored, so she stays in the rhythm.

scenarios.name: A fresh dose after the relapse narrows it, and she is still seizing
scenarios.note: DIPH-09. The dose given after the relapse sets bicarb_after_relapse.

scenarios.name: She does not relapse a second time
scenarios.note: DIPH-09. The relapse rule grants seizure_relapsed and needs it unset, so it fires once.

scenarios.name: A fresh dose and a benzodiazepine after the relapse reach the narrowing phase
scenarios.note: DIPH-09. The benzodiazepine alone does not narrow the relapsed rhythm. The fresh dose does.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate alone in the wide-complex phase, then three minutes still seizing, relapses once
scenarios.note: DIPH-09. The relapse applies to every entry into the seizing phase with bicarbonate and no anticonvulsant.

scenarios.name: Phenytoin on arrival widens her into the wide-complex rhythm
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-23 (Aakash Setty, 27 October 2026), option C. Ten seconds after the drug.

scenarios.name: Phenytoin after the seizure widens her into the wide-complex rhythm
scenarios.note: DIPH-23, from the post-ictal phase.

scenarios.name: After phenytoin on arrival, bicarbonate alone narrows the rhythm and the scheduled seizure comes
scenarios.note: She has not had the seizure yet, so bicarbonate alone takes her to the seizing phase rather than back to arrival. The case keeps the author's scheduled seizure in every run (DIPH-01).

scenarios.name: After phenytoin on arrival, bicarbonate and a benzodiazepine reach the narrowing phase
scenarios.note: The wide-complex rescue needs bicarbonate and an anticonvulsant, whatever the route in.

scenarios.name: Propranolol while the QRS is wide halts the case
scenarios.note: Physician review DIPH-27 (Aakash Setty, 27 October 2026), option B. Propranolol also blocks cardiac sodium channels.

scenarios.name: Propranolol once she has stabilized is discouraged and does not halt the case
scenarios.note: DIPH-27. Harmful in the same phases as physostigmine, discouraged once stabilized.
